facts.subject: Momine Khatun Mausoleum (Möminə Xatun türbəsi), Nakhchivan city. Built 1186 (Euronews 2018; advantour 'April 1186'; Wikipedia Ajami Nakhchivani: date on the walls 1186–1187). Architect Ajami Nakhchivani (Əcəmi Naxçıvani) — Euronews; Wikipedia ('masterpiece of Ajami'). Ten-sided (Wikipedia 'ten-sided'; Euronews '10 decorated facets'; advantour 'decahedral'). Every face covered with ornament and Kufic inscriptions (Wikipedia; advantour). Height today 'more than 25 m' (Wikipedia) / '26 m' (Euronews); originally about 9 m higher with a tent-shaped dome (Euronews: 'originally 9 metres higher'; advantour: 'reaching 34 metres'). Underground burial vault (Wikipedia; advantour). Built in honour of Momine Khatun, wife of Atabeg Shamsaddin Eldaniz (Euronews; Wikipedia says wife of Eldegiz or of his son — so NO family detail in the reel beyond 'Atabəylər dövrü'). 1186 → 2026 = 840 years. NOT used: 'nine of ten sides have different ornaments' (advantour only), who ordered it (sources disagree), UNESCO tentative list (page not verified).

facts.subject: Thor Heyerdahl (Norwegian explorer, Kon-Tiki raft 1947 across the Pacific, ~4 300 miles ≈ 6 900 km — HISTORY.com 'completes 4,300-mile ocean voyage', 7 Aug 1947; died 18 Apr 2002 aged 87 — HISTORY.com). His Azerbaijan theory: an old Icelandic saga says Odin, the Norse god and mythic ancestor of the Vikings, came to Scandinavia from an eastern land called 'Aser' — Heyerdahl linked it to Azerbaijan (NatGeo Out of Eden 2015 '800-year-old Icelandic saga … As-hov or Aser'; Azerbaijan International 8.2). He was drawn by Gobustan petroglyph boats that resemble Scandinavian ones (Azerbaijan International 7.3: 'ship designs … similar'; 8.2: 'petroglyphs that feature reed ships'). Visits: 1980/81, 1994, 1999 (AI 7.3 'third visit'), fourth in Sept 2000 at 86 (AI 8.4). In 2000 he took part in the excavation in Kiş (Shaki); a monument to him stands in Kiş (Wikipedia 'Kiş, Shaki': 'monument to … Thor Heyerdahl, who visited the village during archaeological excavations in 2000'; NatGeo: bronze bust). TWIST (honest): no hard evidence for Norwegian–Azerbaijani ancestry (NatGeo, archaeologist Jeyhun Eminli: 'great traveler … not much of a scientist'); the Gobustan boat engravings are far older than the Vikings — Neolithic (NatGeo); most scholars never embraced his theories (HISTORY.com). NOT used: Kish church origin claims (contested, conflict-adjacent), '101 days' (only from memory — VERIFY at build before using), exact first-visit year (1980 vs 1981).

trend.subject: Riemann hypothesis (Bernhard Riemann, 1859; 1859→2026 = 167 years) — one of the 7 Clay Millennium Prize Problems (2000), $1 million (CASRAI; Hollywood Life; FelloAI; Anthropic 10 Aug page '1859 … million-dollar bounty'). 20 Nov 2026: Levent Alpöge (research scientist / member of technical staff at Anthropic; Harvard Society of Fellows junior fellow — alpo.ge, CASRAI) posted a 4-page note 'Remark' claiming a proof of RH and of GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, made with Claude, as a Lean 4 archive: 175,187 Lean files (CASRAI; FelloAI), ~17.4 million lines (FelloAI; Hollywood Life 'approximately 17 million'), >61.5 GB unpacked (CASRAI). Alpöge: a written-out version 'hit 250,000+ pages' (FelloAI; CASRAI; Hollywood Life). Quote: 'Claude far outpaced me near the finish line' (FelloAI; Hollywood Life). Lean kernel check: Andrew Sutherland (MIT) compiled all modules, accepted 175,187/175,187, only the 3 standard axioms (CASRAI; FelloAI). NOT accepted by mathematicians yet — no human-readable proof; Kontorovich (Rutgers, via AP in Hollywood Life): 'Does that mean I understand it? Not yet.' Clay rules: publication + 2 years of community scrutiny + general acceptance (FelloAI; CASRAI). Background: Alpöge — Turkish-American, born 1992, grew up on Long Island, Harvard 2014 top of his class ('sınıfının birincisi'), Princeton PhD 2020 under Manjul Bhargava (borsagundem.com.tr 10 Sep 2026 'Türk kökenli'; gazeteoksijen.com 'Türk matematikçi'; Harvard + Princeton also on alpo.ge).
